LESSON: READING POSTURE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: Reading
Topic 2.2: Reading posture
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading posture, part of Reading in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need to sit upright as we read?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading posture together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration is enhanced as the learner practices good reading posture to partner with peer assessment

and feedback being given.

• Critical thinking and problem solving is enhanced as the learner learns to sit properly while reading and ensure that there is

no straining in a reading learning experience.

Values:
• Love is developed as the learner together with another demonstrates right sitting posture while doing peer assessment give

one another feedback.

• Unity is developed as the learners work together giving one another feedback on how to use right reading posture.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Health education is enhanced as the learner learns proper sitting posture while reading that helps avoid unnecessary straining of

body parts that could bring about health issues.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Outdoor activities as the learner practices both ross and fine motor muscles in and outside class.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Why do we need to sit upright as we read?
